subject: history_social
passage: Sialkot, Pakistan, produces a large share of the world's hand-stitched soccer balls. Industrial researcher Farhan Qureshi visited a workshop that stitches balls both by hand and with sewing machines and recorded the output of each method over one week. He found that a worker using a machine finished far more balls in a day than a hand stitcher did: ______

data.title: Output of Two Stitching Methods at a Sialkot Workshop
columns: Balls finished per worker per day

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: 5 percent of the machine-stitched balls were rejected for flaws.
choices.B: machine stitchers were paid more per day than hand stitchers.
choices.C: a hand stitcher finished 11 balls per day, compared with 4 for a machine stitcher.
choices.D: a machine stitcher finished 11 balls per day, compared with 4 for a hand stitcher.

explanation.why: The statement compares how many balls each kind of worker finished in a day, so look at the "Balls finished per worker per day" column. Machine stitching shows 11 and hand stitching shows 4.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is accurate, but it describes flaws rather than how many balls were finished.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The table shows the price of each ball, not what the workers were paid.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This swaps the two methods: the machine stitcher is the one who finished 11 balls a day.
explanation.D: Correct. A machine stitcher finished 11 balls a day, nearly three times the 4 finished by a hand stitcher.
